title: Zero seen, zero possible?
hook: A clean test run still leaves uncertainty.

knows: Small arithmetic and the prerequisites listed below.
doesNotKnow: zero observed failures does not identify a zero underlying failure probability; a test bound depends on independent trials and its confidence convention.

misconception: zero observed failures does not identify a zero underlying failure probability; a test bound depends on independent trials and its confidence convention.
objective: zero observed failures does not identify a zero underlying failure probability; a test bound depends on independent trials and its confidence convention.

claims.text: Independent Bernoulli trials give P(zero)=(1-p)^n. Solve P(zero)=.05 for upper=1-.05^(1/n). At n100,p.01 zero probability is .366032; upper .029513. One duplicated underlying observation has effective n1, zero chance .99 and endpoint .95. n200 endpoint .014867. Curve samples this likelihood, not a posterior density.

Exact local derivation, not independent verification.

claims.text: Title: Zero seen, zero possible? Hook: A clean test run still leaves uncertainty. 100 independent tests show no failures. Could the true failure rate still be 1%? Options: Yes / No; answer 0.

claims.text: For the retained independent-test model, a 1% failure rate still gives about 36.6% chance of zero failures in 100 tests. The one-sided 95% zero-failure endpoint is about 2.95%, not zero. Duplicated observations count as one independent trial, so the same inference does not apply.
